results.reader_title: Research funding and citation impact differ across national systems
results.reader_what: Dutch NWO-funded publications outperform other funded publications on citation measures; German DFG results differ.
results.reader_why: Funding arrangements and collaboration interact differently across national research systems.
results.reader_more: The six-country study uses Web of Science data from 2009–2016 and regression analysis. Germany and the Netherlands are substantive country cases, with distinct results across fields. Citation impact is not equivalent to scientific quality or proof of a funding agency’s causal effect.

deep_analysis.research_question: How do national research funding and international collaboration relate to citation impact?
deep_analysis.main_finding: NWO-funded papers show stronger citation performance than other funded Dutch papers, whereas DFG-funded German papers do not show the same overall advantage.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Author-uploaded matching article text, Web of Science 2009–2016, field-normalised citation measures and OLS regressions.
deep_analysis.qualification: Historical observational bibliometrics; selection and disciplinary composition limit causal interpretation.
